name: Earthcore

influenced_by: cottagecore and goblincore's nature-adjacent internet-aesthetic wave
a post-pandemic surge of interest in pottery, foraging and other tactile, slow crafts

reacts_against: the bright, saturated palettes common to many other internet aesthetics, insisting on an unglamorous, literally dirt-toned color range instead.
article: Earthcore names a 2020s internet-aesthetic tag built around a deliberately unglamorous palette — clay, stone, moss, raw soil — applied across fashion and interiors as a mineral, muted counterpoint to brighter internet aesthetics. It emerged as part of a broader cluster of nature-adjacent "core" tags (alongside cottagecore and goblincore) that gained momentum during and after pandemic-era lockdowns, when renewed interest in gardening, pottery, foraging and other slow, tactile crafts fed directly into online aesthetic communities looking for a visual language to match. Earthcore's boundary against goblincore (messier, more amphibian) and wabi-sabi (Japanese, philosophically grounded, much older) is genuinely loose — like several recent internet-aesthetic tags, it functions more as a palette descriptor shared across several related communities than as a single, sharply bounded movement with its own independent history.

findings: mostly muted — about 90% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from Wikimedia Commons images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
